items.title: fix(cron): spawn-only jobs fail when the subagent is spawned with cle…
items.summary: fix(cron): spawn-only jobs fail when the subagent is spawned with cleanup delete (#162962) ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: a scheduled job whose agent hands the work to one subagent fails with "cron child-session handoff completed without a final assistant payload" when the agent spawns that subagent with `cleanup: "delete"`. ## User Impact User impact: spawn-only cron jobs deliver the subagent's report, whatever `cleanup` value the model picks. Before this change, most `cleanup: "delete"` runs failed even though the subagent had finished its work. ## Why This Change Was Made A cron run reads its subagent's result from the subagent registry row after the subagent settles (#117308; #162474 added the `delivery: none` path). The registry retires a `cleanup: "delete"` row as soon as the requester settle wake finishes. For a cron requester, that wake completes immediately because nothing wakes a cron run (#99396, #135318). The row was gone about 1 s after the child ended, and the cron run reads about 5 s later, so it found nothing. The fix is in the subagent registry, which owns the row lifetime: - A child whose requester is a cron run is not retired on settle for `cleanup: "delete"`. The child session is still deleted right after the announce, as before; only the registry row stays until the normal archive sweep (`archiveAfterMinutes`, default 60). - That child's handoff delivery is recorded as terminal (`not_required` with disposition `intentional_non_delivery`) instead of `pending`. A pending handoff would block the archive sweep, so this keeps the row from leaking. Nothing ever delivered to a cron run requester here anyway. Owner decision (retention): the maintainer accepted bounded retention for this case. A cron run's child row is not retired on settle; it stays until the normal archive sweep and is not held for the cron run's lifetime. A row whose result was already captured lasts at most `archiveAfterMinutes` (or the 5-minute run TTL when archiving is off). That is the archive deadline the registry already sets on `cleanup: "delete"` rows (`archiveAtMs`); this change only stops the earlier retirement on settle. No new storage, schema or field is added. Invariants kept: non-cron `delete` rows still retire on settle (#99396). Killed children still retire on settle. Collector rows are unchanged. The cron settle-wake shortcut still runs. No new messages or warnings. Alternatives rejected: making the settle wake wait for the cron run to end inverts ownership and holds gateway drain. Polling faster in cron is still a race. Treating cron children as swarm collectors (`collect`) would also change concurrency slots, structured output and kill handling. Hermes comparison: Hermes joins delegated children synchronously when the session has no consumer for later results (cron included), so this race cannot happen there. OpenClaw's cron spawn-only handoff is asynchronous by design (#117308), so the fix keeps the result where the cron run reads it. ## Evidence - Regression test (`subagent-registry.requester-wake.e2e.test.ts`) drives the real registry and the real cron reader (`readDescendantSubagentFallbackReply`). A `cleanup: "delete"` child of a cron run settles, its settle wake completes, and the cron read returns the child's answer. The sweeper then removes the row, and no announce or agent turn starts at any point. The test runs two cases: - Archiving enabled (`archiveAfterMinutes: 1`), no restart. The row is retired at the archive deadline. - Archiving disabled (`archiveAfterMinutes: 0`), with a registry restart between the settle and the read. The row is restored from SQLite, it is still readable, and it is retired after the 5-minute run TTL. Nothing is replayed. - Without the retirement change, the cron read returns `undefined` (the live failure). - Without the delivery change, the row is never swept (`expected { runId, … } to be undefined`). - With both changes, the test passes. - CI on `cd5c3796304`: every type, lint, guard and node lane passes, including `check-test-types-core-1..5` and `check-prod-types`. The only red lane is `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway (1/2)`, in `ui/src/e2e/model-catalog-partial-refresh.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`. The same test fails on unrelated PRs in the same window (runs 36924844797, 36924235817, 36926791756, 36927139856, 36927939720). It passes locally on this head, and this PR touches no UI or model-catalog code. - The full `subagent-registry.requester-wake.e2e.test.ts` file passes (27 tests). It took 60.9 s wall time, with Vitest reporting 58.4 s; each new case takes about 0.8 s. - Neighboring suites pass: lifecycle, registry, persistence, sweeper lifecycle, cron subagent follow-up (unit and worker), and announce timeout (417 tests). - Live, real `gpt-6-astra` (Telegram Test Server userbot harness with a pass-through proxy to the real OpenAI API). There were 10 spawn-only announce cron runs per side, and the parent was told to spawn with `cleanup: "delete"`. All 10 spawns per side used `cleanup: "delete"`. - Before, on origin/main `4f0541eb469`: 9 of 10 runs failed with "cron child-session handoff completed without a final assistant payload". Only 1 of 10 child reports reached the Telegram chat. - After, on this head (fix commit `d15345587a1`; later commits only change the test): 0 of 10 handoff failures, and all 10 child reports reached the Telegram chat. - The child has no shell tool in this harness, so its report is an `AUTOMATION_FAILED` message and the job status is `error` on purpose. The run shows the cron run receiving and delivering the child's own answer instead of the handoff error. ## Bounded cost - Per cron run child with `cleanup: "delete"`: one registry row (already persisted) lives until the archive sweep instead of ~1 s after settle. That is bounded by `agents.defaults.subagents.archiveAfterMinutes` (default 60), or by the 5-minute run TTL when archiving is disabled. - No new timers, waits, polling, model calls or messages. The child session is still deleted at announce time. ## LOC (vs origin/main) Production +11 / -2, tests +67 (net).

items.title: ci: reduce published-driver PR validation cost (#162965)
items.summary: ci: reduce published-driver PR validation cost (#162965) The published-driver update cell ran serially after build-artifacts on every PR it was selected for, adding about 13.5 minutes of critical path. PR selection is now limited to the updater, activation, managed-service handoff, and canary-emitter owners (scheduled main and release validation still run the cell unconditionally); published-install caches have main-only writers with explicit cache-mode gating and read-only PR consumers; PR runs skip initial Doctor seeding and use shorter readiness waits. PR-mode cell measured at 3m32s with a cold image-builder cache. The cleanup tests no longer touch host Docker.

items.title: Google發表Gemini 4 Argon，輸出上限增至100萬個Token
items.summary: Google周三（9/30）發表新一代AI模型Gemini 4 Argon，主攻複雜、長時間工作流程，輸出上限達100萬個Token，較先前Gemini模型的6.4萬個Token大幅提高。目前Argon先透過Fairwind Program提供給一批受信任的資安防禦人員測試，之後才會逐步擴大開放。

items.title: 因應PQC簽章帶來的憑證架構負擔，Cloudflare完成初步大規模MTC實測，已傳送數十億份憑證
items.summary: 由於PQC簽章體積遠大於傳統簽章，恐將增加既有憑證架構負擔，今年2月底Google與Cloudflare合作展開默克樹憑證（Merkle Tree Certificates，MTC）可行性測試，期望透過新的憑證架構與驗證機制加以改善這項問題。

items.title: Microsoft強化Entra ID登入驗證流程，阻擋外部指令碼注入
items.summary: Microsoft將自10月中旬起，強制在Entra ID瀏覽器登入流程實施強化版內容安全性原則（Content Security Policy，CSP），預計10月底前完成。在這項新政策下，僅允許來自受信任Microsoft CDN網域的指令碼執行，阻擋外部或未授權程式碼注入，以降低跨站指令碼（XSS）等攻擊竊取認證資訊的風險。

items.title: 商用逾30年C++編譯器前端EDG開源，C++ Alliance接手維護
items.summary: 老牌C/C++編譯器技術供應商Edison Design Group（EDG）正式公開C/C++編譯器前端原始碼，結束逾30年的專有授權模式。後續專案由非營利組織C++ Alliance接手維護，既有EDG開發人員也會繼續參與，原始碼目前已公開在GitHub。 EDG的C++編譯器前端自1992年推出，而編譯器前端主要負責程式碼編譯的前置工作，負責處理語法、型別和程式結構，再把分析結果交給後續的編譯或開發工具使用。因此EDG前端不像GCC或Clang主要供一般開發者直接作為編譯工具使用，而是提供給其他軟體業者整合進自家產品。

items.title: 中國駭客UAT-11587於亞洲多國政府散布後門Antino，其中包含臺灣
items.summary: 9月30日思科威脅情報團隊Talos揭露鎖定亞洲各國政府機關、參與制訂政策組織的網路間諜活動，攻擊範圍橫跨臺灣、印度、菲律賓、柬埔寨等國，其共通點是攻擊者會使用以Rust打造的後門程式Antino。相關活動最早可追蹤至2025年9月，截至今年7月，已有位於16個組織受害或是遭到鎖定，這些組織分布於包含臺灣在內的8個亞洲國家。
